title: Prefix-Parity Proof Satisfies Every Check
statement: Let $m\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $w$ be a Boolean word of length $m+2$ with odd weight. Define the proof word $q$ of length $m+1$ by taking its $j$th bit to encode, in $\mathbb{F}_2$, the parity of the first $j+2$ bits of $w$. Then every seed $s\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\sqcup\mathrm{Fin}(m)$ specifies a partial-sum check that holds for $w$ and $q$.
hypotheses_covered: $w$ is a Boolean word of length $m+2$
